summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain, following a recent hospitalization for similar symptoms. She has a complex history including chronic graft-versus-host disease, gastroparesis, and immunosuppression. Initial evaluation revealed metabolic acidosis and leukocytosis. Imaging showed no acute abdominal pathology but mild colitis on MRI. Stool testing confirmed rotavirus infection, explaining her gastroenteritis. She also had a complicated UTI with Enterococcus, treated with nitrofurantoin. During her stay, she received IV fluids, antiemetics, and supportive care, with gradual improvement. She tolerated oral intake, and symptoms resolved. A sacral bone marrow finding on MRI prompted a recommendation for outpatient pelvic MRI to rule out infiltrative disease. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans, including completing antibiotics, restarting bowel regimen when appropriate, and coordinating outpatient imaging and IVIG.
